        const rect = element.getBoundingClientRect();
        if (!viewportHeight || rect.height >= viewportHeight) return;
        const y = rect.top + rect.height / 2;
        const hit = y >= 0 && y < viewportHeight
            ? element.ownerDocument.elementFromPoint(rect.left + rect.width / 2, y)
            : null;
        if (!hit || !element.contains(hit)) {
          element.scrollIntoView({block: 'center', inline: 'nearest'});
        }
      })();

  const vec3 yuvOffset = vec3(0.0625, 0.5, 0.5);

}

  function plainObject(value) {
    if (value == null) return {};
    if (!value || typeof value !== 'object' || Array.isArray(value)) return {};
    try {
      var copy = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value));
      return copy && typeof copy === 'object' && !Array.isArray(copy) ? copy : {};

  function postNow(event) {

  function flushPendingEvents() {

    }

  }

function widgetContentHeight() {
  var wrapper = document.getElementById('scroll-wrapper');
  var root = document.getElementById('root');
  return Math.ceil(Math.max(
    elementHeight(root),
    elementHeight(wrapper)
  ));
}

function elementHeight(el) {
  if (!el) return 0;
  var rectHeight = 0;
  if (typeof el.getBoundingClientRect === 'function') {
    try {
      var rect = el.getBoundingClientRect();
      if (rect && typeof rect.height === 'number') {
        rectHeight = Math.ceil(rect.height);
      }
    } catch(e) {}
  }
  return Math.max(
    rectHeight,
    typeof el.scrollHeight === 'number' ? el.scrollHeight : 0,
    typeof el.offsetHeight === 'number' ? el.offsetHeight : 0,
    typeof el.clientHeight === 'number' ? el.clientHeight : 0
  );
}

function reportWidgetHeight() {
  var height = widgetContentHeight();
  if (height > 0 && Math.abs(height - _lastReportedHeight) > 1) {
    _lastReportedHeight = height;
    postToHost({ type: 'chat-widget-height', height: height });
  }
}

function scheduleWidgetHeightReports() {
  if (_heightReportScheduled) return;
  _heightReportScheduled = true;
  var run = function() {
    _heightReportScheduled = false;
    reportWidgetHeight();
  };
  if (window.requestAnimationFrame) {
    window.requestAnimationFrame(run);
  } else {
    setTimeout(run, 16);
  }
}

function installWidgetHeightObserver() {
  if (!window.ResizeObserver) return;
  try {
    _widgetHeightObserver = new ResizeObserver(function() { scheduleWidgetHeightReports(); });
    var wrapper = document.getElementById('scroll-wrapper');
    var root = document.getElementById('root');
    if (wrapper) _widgetHeightObserver.observe(wrapper);
    if (root) _widgetHeightObserver.observe(root);
  } catch(e) {}
}

function osPrefersDark() {
  try {
    return window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches;
  } catch(e) {
    return false;
  }
}

function syncMediaOverrides() {
  for (var d = 0; d < _disabledMediaRules.length; d++) {
    try {
      _disabledMediaRules[d].rule.media.mediaText = _disabledMediaRules[d].orig;
    } catch(e) {}
  }
  _disabledMediaRules = [];

  if (_promotedThemeStyle) {
    _promotedThemeStyle.remove();
    _promotedThemeStyle = null;
  }

  var isDark = _theme === 'dark';
  var osIsDark = osPrefersDark();
  if (isDark === osIsDark) return;

  var unwanted = osIsDark ? 'dark' : 'light';
  var wanted = isDark ? 'dark' : 'light';
  var promoted = [];

  try {
    for (var s = 0; s < document.styleSheets.length; s++) {
      try {
        var rules = document.styleSheets[s].cssRules;
        for (var r = 0; r < rules.length; r++) {
          var rule = rules[r];
          if (rule.type === 4) {
            var mediaText = rule.media.mediaText || '';
            if (mediaText.indexOf('prefers-color-scheme') !== -1) {
              if (mediaText.indexOf(unwanted) !== -1) {
                var original = mediaText;
                rule.media.mediaText = mediaText.replace(/prefers-color-scheme/g, 'prefers-color-scheme-disabled');
                _disabledMediaRules.push({rule: rule, orig: original});
              }
              if (mediaText.indexOf(wanted) !== -1) {
                for (var i = 0; i < rule.cssRules.length; i++) {
                  promoted.push(rule.cssRules[i].cssText);
                }
              }
            }
          }
        }
      } catch(e) {}
    }
  } catch(e) {}

  if (promoted.length) {
    _promotedThemeStyle = document.createElement('style');
    _promotedThemeStyle.id = 'theme-promoted';
    _promotedThemeStyle.textContent = promoted.join('');
    document.body.appendChild(_promotedThemeStyle);
  }
}

function applyHostCssVariables(cssVariables) {
  if (typeof cssVariables !== 'string' || !cssVariables) return;
  _hostCssVariables = cssVariables;
  cssVariables.split(';').forEach(function(part) {
    var index = part.indexOf(':');
    if (index <= 0) return;
    var name = part.slice(0, index).trim();
    var value = part.slice(index + 1).trim();
    if (name.indexOf('--') !== 0 || !value) return;
    document.documentElement.style.setProperty(name, value);
  });
}

function applyTheme(theme, cssVariables) {
  _theme = theme === 'dark' ? 'dark' : 'light';
  var isDark = _theme === 'dark';
  var colorScheme = isDark ? 'dark' : 'light';
  document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme', colorScheme);
  document.body.setAttribute('data-theme', colorScheme);
  if (_declareColorScheme) {
    document.documentElement.style.colorScheme = colorScheme;
    document.body.style.colorScheme = colorScheme;
    var colorSchemeMeta = document.querySelector('meta[name="color-scheme"]');
    if (colorSchemeMeta) {
      colorSchemeMeta.setAttribute('content', colorScheme);
    }
  }
  applyHostCssVariables(cssVariables || _hostCssVariables);
  syncMediaOverrides();
}

// State sync handler (called from native)
function updateWidgetState(stateJson, stateVersion) {
  try {
    if (typeof stateVersion === 'number' && stateVersion >= 0) {
      _widgetStateVersion = Math.floor(stateVersion);
      if (_widgetStateVersion > 0) _widgetStateInitialized = true;
    }
    _widgetState = plainWidgetState(JSON.parse(stateJson));
    emitWidgetState();
    scheduleWidgetHeightReports();
  } catch(e) {}
}

// Theme sync handler (called from native)
function updateTheme(theme) {
  applyTheme(theme, arguments.length > 1 ? arguments[1] : _hostCssVariables);
  scheduleWidgetHeightReports();
}
</script>

          function resolveCurrentSpacePathPrefix() {
            var currentPath = window.location.pathname || "";
            if (currentPath.indexOf(spacesRoutePrefix) !== 0) {
              return null;
            }

            var relativePath = currentPath.slice(spacesRoutePrefix.length);
            var slashIndex = relativePath.indexOf("/");
            if (slashIndex <= 0) {
              return null;
            }

            return spacesRoutePrefix + relativePath.slice(0, slashIndex + 1);
          }

          function rewriteSpacesUrl(urlLike) {
            if (!urlLike) {
              return urlLike;
            }

            var url;
            try {
              url = new URL(String(urlLike), window.location.href);
            } catch (e) {
              return urlLike;
            }

            if (url.origin !== window.location.origin) {
              return urlLike;
            }

            if (!url.pathname || url.pathname.indexOf(spacesRoutePrefix) !== 0) {
              return urlLike;
            }

            var currentSpacePathPrefix = resolveCurrentSpacePathPrefix();
            var relativePath = url.pathname.slice(spacesRoutePrefix.length);
            if (
              currentSpacePathPrefix &&
              url.pathname.indexOf(currentSpacePathPrefix) !== 0 &&
              relativePath &&
              relativePath.indexOf("/") === -1 &&
              nestedSpaceEndpoints[relativePath]
            ) {
              url.pathname = currentSpacePathPrefix + relativePath;
            }

            return url.toString();
          }

          function isSpacesOriginUrl(urlLike) {
            try {
              var u = new URL(String(urlLike), window.location.href);
              return u.origin === window.location.origin &&
                     u.pathname &&
                     u.pathname.indexOf(spacesRoutePrefix) === 0;
            } catch (e) { return false; }
          }

          function __fwaB64ToBytes(b64) {
            var bin = atob(b64 || "");
            var len = bin.length;
            var bytes = new Uint8Array(len);
            for (var i = 0; i < len; i++) bytes[i] = bin.charCodeAt(i);

          function __fwaBytesToB64(bytes) {
            var bin = "";
            var CHUNK = 0x8000;
            for (var i = 0; i < bytes.length; i += CHUNK) {
              bin += String.fromCharCode.apply(null, bytes.subarray(i, i + CHUNK));
            }
            return btoa(bin);
          }

            navigator.sendBeacon = function(url, data) {
              return originalSendBeacon(rewriteSpacesUrl(url), data);
            };
          }

          return true;
        } catch (e) {
          return false;
        }
      })();

  _widgetFocusUserInitiated = false;

window.__hatchSuspendAutomaticFocus = function() {
  _widgetFocusUserInitiated = false;
  var active = document.activeElement;
  if (active && active !== document.body && typeof active.blur === 'function') {
    active.blur();

['pointerdown', 'touchstart', 'keydown', 'click'].forEach(function(type) {

window.open = function(url) {
  try {
    var target = url ? new URL(url, location.href) : null;
    if (target && /^(https?|mailto|tel|sms|geo):$/.test(target.protocol)) {
      location.assign(target.href);
    }
  } catch (e) {}
  return null;
};

// domStorageEnabled is false on this WebView, so unguarded localStorage access
// throws and kills the widget script mid-render. Mirror the Hatch web shell's
// in-memory polyfill so such widgets degrade to per-load state instead of dying.
(function() {
  var needsPolyfill = false;
  try {
    var probe = window.localStorage;
    if (!probe) {
      needsPolyfill = true;
    } else {
      probe.setItem('__hatch_storage_probe__', '1');
      probe.removeItem('__hatch_storage_probe__');
    }
  } catch (e) {
    needsPolyfill = true;
  }
  if (!needsPolyfill) return;
  var memoryStorage = function(s) {
    return {
      getItem: function(k) { return Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(s, k) ? s[k] : null; },
      setItem: function(k, v) { s[k] = String(v); },
      removeItem: function(k) { delete s[k]; },
      clear: function() { for (var k in s) delete s[k]; },
      key: function(i) { return Object.keys(s)[i] || null; },
      get length() { return Object.keys(s).length; }
    };
  };
  try {
    Object.defineProperty(window, 'localStorage', { value: memoryStorage({}), configurable: true });
    Object.defineProperty(window, 'sessionStorage', { value: memoryStorage({}), configurable: true });
  } catch (e) {}
})();

function postToHost(message) {
  var bridge = window.HatchBridge;
  if (!bridge || !bridge.postMessage) return;
  bridge.postMessage(JSON.stringify(message));
}

function verticalScrollRoom(target) {
  var room = { up: false, down: false };
  for (var el = target; el && el.nodeType === 1 && el !== document.body; el = el.parentElement) {
    var overflowY = getComputedStyle(el).overflowY;
    if ((overflowY === 'auto' || overflowY === 'scroll') && el.scrollHeight > el.clientHeight + 1) {
      if (el.scrollTop > 0) room.up = true;
      if (el.scrollTop + el.clientHeight < el.scrollHeight - 1) room.down = true;
    }
  }
  return room;
}

document.addEventListener('touchstart', function(event) {
  var room = verticalScrollRoom(event.target);
  postToHost({ type: 'chat-widget-touch', can_scroll_up: room.up, can_scroll_down: room.down });
}, { capture: true, passive: true });

function postWidgetState() {
  postToHost({
    type: 'chat-widget-state',
    action: 'set_state',
    state: copyWidgetState()
  });
}

function scheduleWidgetStatePost() {
  if (_widgetStatePostScheduled) return;
  _widgetStatePostScheduled = true;
  setTimeout(function() {
    _widgetStatePostScheduled = false;
    postWidgetState();
  }, 0);
}

function plainWidgetState(value) {
  if (!value || typeof value !== 'object' || Array.isArray(value)) {
    return {};
  }
  try {
    var copy = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value));
    return copy && typeof copy === 'object' && !Array.isArray(copy) ? copy : {};
  } catch(e) {
    return {};
  }
}

function copyWidgetState() {
  return plainWidgetState(_widgetState);
}

function parseInitialWidgetState(stateJson) {
  try {
    return plainWidgetState(JSON.parse(stateJson));
  } catch(e) {
    return {};
  }
}

function writeWidgetState(state) {
  var nextState = plainWidgetState(state);
  _widgetState = nextState;
  _widgetStateInitialized = true;
  emitWidgetState();
  scheduleWidgetStatePost();
}

function emitWidgetState() {
  try {
    window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('hatch-widget-state', {
      detail: { state: copyWidgetState() }
    }));
  } catch(e) {}
}

// Public widget API. Mirrors the Hatch web shell so widget HTML can call
// window.hatchWidget.getState() and setState(...).
window.hatchWidget = {
  getState: function(defaults) {
    if (
      arguments.length > 0 &&
      _widgetStateVersion === 0 &&
      !_widgetStateInitialized &&
      defaults &&
      typeof defaults === 'object' &&
      !Array.isArray(defaults)
    ) {
      writeWidgetState(defaults);
    }
    return copyWidgetState();
  },
  setState: function(state) { writeWidgetState(state); }
};

       not the body's width. Generous padding gives descenders / italic overhang and
       KaTeX's negative-margin tricks (limits, accents) room before the captured bounds. */
    #container { display: inline-block; padding: 6px 12px; white-space: nowrap; }
    /* KaTeX block math defaults to display:block, which expands to parent width and centers
       — we want the actual content width, so override. */

  <script>
    function renderKatex(expression, displayMode, textColor, density, fontSizeSp) {
      try {
        if (typeof katex === 'undefined') {
          KatexBridge.onRenderError('katex not loaded');
          return;
        }
        var container = document.getElementById('container');
        container.innerHTML = '';
        container.style.color = textColor;
        // Set the CSS font-size for the math container. KaTeX's stylesheet sets
        // `.katex { font-size: 1.21em }`, which scales the rendered glyphs to ~1.21x
        // the input — so passing the surrounding text's size as-is would yield math
        // glyphs visibly larger than the body text. Divide by 1.21 here so the
        // rendered glyph cap height matches the body text's; callers can keep passing
        // the surrounding font size directly without being aware of KaTeX's internal
        // scaling. Also: the WebView's CSS-to-device-px mapping is 1 CSS px = density
        // device px (so 16 CSS px = 48 device px on xxhdpi); we compensate for that
        // by multiplying the measured CSS-px dimensions by `density` below when
        // bridging back to Android.
        var KATEX_INTRINSIC_SCALE = 1.21;
        var effectiveFontPx = (fontSizeSp || 16) / KATEX_INTRINSIC_SCALE;
        container.style.fontSize = effectiveFontPx + 'px';
        katex.render(expression, container, {
          displayMode: displayMode,
          output: 'html',
          throwOnError: false,
          strict: 'ignore',
        });
        // KaTeX loads its math fonts (KaTeX_*.woff2) asynchronously. If we measure
        // immediately, the layout is computed with fallback metrics → reported size is
        // wrong → the bitmap captures a smaller region than the final rendered content.
        // document.fonts.ready resolves once all @font-face fonts referenced by the
        // current DOM have downloaded; one rAF after that ensures the post-load layout
        // has been committed before we measure.
        var fontsReady = (document.fonts && document.fonts.ready)
          ? document.fonts.ready
          : Promise.resolve();
        fontsReady.then(function() {
          requestAnimationFrame(function() {
            // Measure the `.katex` (inline) or `.katex-display` (block) root element
            // directly, then add fixed overhang padding to capture KaTeX's negative-
            // margin glyphs (limits above big operators, accents, sqrt extenders).
            //
            // Why not union descendant bounds? KaTeX's HTML output contains `.vlist` and
            // `.strut` elements whose `getBoundingClientRect` reports widths far beyond
            // the actual painted content (vertical-layout helpers with absolute children
            // that float to extreme positions). Unioning them inflated bitmaps to
            // thousands of pixels of empty whitespace flanking a tiny strip of math.
            // The .katex root's own bounds are tight to the visible glyph stack; the
            // overhang padding is a small constant that handles the negative-margin
            // ascenders/descenders without picking up off-flow helpers.
            var katexRoot =
                container.querySelector('.katex-display') ||
                container.querySelector('.katex');
            if (!katexRoot) {
              KatexBridge.onRenderError('katex root element not found after render');
              return;
            }
            var rect = katexRoot.getBoundingClientRect();
            var OVERHANG_TOP = 8;
            var OVERHANG_BOTTOM = 4;
            var OVERHANG_X = 4;
            // Multiply CSS-px values by density to convert to device px. The WebView
            // paints content at density-scaled positions on its drawing surface, so the
            // captured Bitmap (allocated in device px and filled by wv.draw(canvas))
            // must use device-px dimensions to encompass the full painted area.
            var d = density || 1;
            var offsetX = Math.floor((rect.left - OVERHANG_X) * d);
            var offsetY = Math.floor((rect.top - OVERHANG_TOP) * d);
            var width = Math.ceil((rect.width + OVERHANG_X * 2) * d);
            var height = Math.ceil((rect.height + OVERHANG_TOP + OVERHANG_BOTTOM) * d);
            KatexBridge.onMeasured(offsetX, offsetY, width, height);
          });
        });
      } catch(e) {
        KatexBridge.onRenderError(e.message || 'Unknown error');
      }
    }
  </script>

Active notifications surfaced by the system notification listener. Each entry has `app`, `app_package`, `title`, `body`, `sender`, `category` (one of msg, email, social, call, missed_call, other — `call` is a placed or in-progress call, `missed_call` is one the user missed; never treat them as the same thing), and `dedup_key` (a stable id for the same physical message across re-emissions — use it to avoid reporting a notification twice). In messaging notifications, `sender` identifies each message's author, including the user's own replies. `title` labels the notification or conversation, not necessarily the sender. For when it arrived use `timestamp_local` (the user's local wall-clock time), `timestamp_local_date` (their local calendar day), and `timestamp_weekday` (their local weekday name). `timestamp` is UTC and internal — NEVER show it to the user and never use it to compute the day, date, or weekday: it names the wrong day for notifications that arrived in the evening. Show the weekday using `timestamp_weekday` verbatim.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `Dependency` (`work_spec_id` TEXT NOT NULL, `prerequisite_id` TEXT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY(`work_spec_id`, `prerequisite_id`), FOREIGN KEY(`work_spec_id`) REFERENCES `WorkSpec`(`id`) ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE CASCADE , FOREIGN KEY(`prerequisite_id`) REFERENCES `WorkSpec`(`id`) ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE CASCADE )
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `Preference` (`key` TEXT NOT NULL, `long_value` INTEGER, PRIMARY KEY(`key`))
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `SystemIdInfo` (`work_spec_id` TEXT NOT NULL, `generation` INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, `system_id` INTEGER NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY(`work_spec_id`, `generation`), FOREIGN KEY(`work_spec_id`) REFERENCES `WorkSpec`(`id`) ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE CASCADE )

Create VideoEncoderSession: 
Create a new calendar event. `calendar_id` is optional. Only pass it when a matching calendar ID is available in the current `calendars` array published by the `calendar` data source. Do not guess calendar IDs and do not reuse stale IDs from memory; omit `calendar_id` when unsure, when no calendar preference was requested, or when the current data-source payload does not contain a matching calendar. When `calendar_id` is omitted or stale, Android creates the event in the best visible, syncing writable calendar available. Picking a calendar: (1) if the user names a provider in the canonical list ('Google', 'Outlook', 'Samsung', 'Yahoo', 'Exchange', 'iCloud', 'Fastmail', 'Proton'), filter the `calendars` array by the matching `provider` field. Within those filtered results, prefer calendars with `is_owner_account=true` AND `is_primary=true` (the user's own primary calendar) over shared/group calendars like Google 'Family' or subscribed calendars — only pick a non-owner calendar if the user explicitly names it (e.g. 'Family calendar', 'work shared calendar'). Do NOT fall back on is_primary across providers in this case. (2) if the user names a provider not in the canonical list, do a case-insensitive substring match of the spoken name against `account_type`, `account_name`, and `display_name` and pick from any matches; (3) if the user names an account by email, match on account_name; (4) only if the user gives no signal, pick the calendar with `is_owner_account=true` AND `is_primary=true`, preferring Google > Outlook > Exchange > iCloud > Yahoo > Samsung. On Samsung devices is_primary often points at a Samsung system calendar the user does not actively use, and a Google account auto-creates a 'Family' group calendar — neither should be the default pick when ambiguous. Use this for requests like 'Schedule a meeting at 3pm', 'Add lunch with Sarah to my calendar', 'Block off tomorrow morning'. To create a repeating event (e.g. 'every night at 10pm', 'every weekday standup'), pass an iCalendar `rrule` such as 'FREQ=DAILY' or 'FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,TU,WE,TH,FR'; a recurring event sets its length with `duration` (ISO-8601, e.g. 'PT1H', default 1 hour) and must NOT also pass `end_time`. Always pass `events_json`, a JSON array string of event objects, even for one event. Each object must include `title` and `start_time`; optional per-event fields are `calendar_id`, `end_time`, `description`, `location`, `all_day`, `timezone`, `reminder_minutes`, `rrule`, and `duration`.

Device calendars and events (id, title, start/end time, location, provider). `start_date`/`end_date` are UTC and for internal use only — NEVER show them to the user and never use them to compute the day, date, or weekday. Display the date/time from the local fields instead: for a timed event (`is_all_day`=false) use `start_local`/`end_local` (the event's local wall-clock time); for an all-day event (`is_all_day`=true) use `start_local_date` (first day) through `end_local_date` (last day, INCLUSIVE) — note the UTC `end_date` is exclusive (midnight after the last day) and must not be shown. If `start_local_date` equals `end_local_date` it is a single all-day day. Always show the weekday using the provided `start_weekday`/`end_weekday` verbatim; never derive the weekday yourself.
Device call log entries. Each entry has `number`, `name` (the contact name cached by the phone, may be null), and `direction` — one of incoming, outgoing, missed, voicemail, rejected, blocked, answered_externally. `direction` is the ONLY authoritative source for whether the user placed, received, or missed a call; outgoing means the user made the call. For when the call happened use `date_local` (the user's local wall-clock time), `date_local_date` (their local calendar day), and `date_weekday` (their local weekday name). `type` and `date` are raw internal values — `type` is an Android enum integer and `date` is UTC epoch milliseconds. NEVER show either to the user, never fall back to `type` to determine direction, and never use `date` to compute the day or weekday: it names the wrong day for calls made in the evening. `duration` is in SECONDS. An entry records only that a call occurred; it carries no information about what the call was about.

In-app alarms (set on devices with no clock app) are dismissed directly; alarms in the device's clock app are dismissed via that app. Use this for requests like 'Dismiss my alarm', 'Cancel the 7am alarm', 'Turn off the alarm'. Always pass `targets_json`, a JSON array string of target objects, even for one alarm. Each object must include `alarm_id` or `message`.

Dismiss every scheduled ALARM on the device at once (reminders are NOT affected — use reminder.dismiss_all for those). Use this for requests like 'cancel all my alarms', 'clear my alarms', 'remove every alarm'. For a single specific alarm use alarm.dismiss instead. EmojiCompat is not initialized.

You must initialize EmojiCompat prior to referencing the EmojiCompat instance.

The most likely cause of this error is disabling the EmojiCompatInitializer
either explicitly in AndroidManifest.xml, or by including
androidx.emoji2:emoji2-bundled.

Automatic initialization is typically performed by EmojiCompatInitializer. If
you are not expecting to initialize EmojiCompat manually in your application,
please check to ensure it has not been removed from your APK's manifest. You can
do this in Android Studio using Build > Analyze APK.

In the APK Analyzer, ensure that the startup entry for
EmojiCompatInitializer and InitializationProvider is present in
 AndroidManifest.xml. If it is missing or contains tools:node="remove", and you
intend to use automatic configuration, verify:

  1. Your application does not include emoji2-bundled
  2. All modules do not contain an exclusion manifest rule for
     EmojiCompatInitializer or InitializationProvider. For more information
     about manifest exclusions see the documentation for the androidx startup
     library.

If you intend to use emoji2-bundled, please call EmojiCompat.init. You can
learn more in the documentation for BundledEmojiCompatConfig.

If you intended to perform manual configuration, it is recommended that you call
EmojiCompat.init immediately on application startup.

If you still cannot resolve this issue, please open a bug with your specific
configuration to help improve error message.

Hatch-created alarms mirrored from the system Clock app (id, label, time, recurrence). Read them with `alarm.list`. On a recurring alarm, use `days_weekdays` (a list of full weekday names) to say which days it runs. `days` is a raw CSV of Java Calendar constants where 1=Sunday through 7=Saturday — NOT the ISO numbering where 1=Monday — so never interpret it yourself or the alarm will be reported one day late.

Health Connect SDK is not available on this device.
Health Connect data (aggregates, workouts, sleep, events) pushed via observer-driven background sync. Time fields on these rows are epoch SECONDS, not milliseconds — `start_epoch_sec`/`end_epoch_sec`, and `start_ts`/`end_ts` on raw samples, which are the same unit despite the shorter name. Every other Hatch data source sends milliseconds, so do not compare these to another source's timestamps without accounting for the 1000x difference. Rows also carry `timezone`, a UTC OFFSET such as "-07:00" or "Z" (never an IANA region name); use it to place a record in the user's local day rather than reading the epoch value as UTC.

HelpTicketTopics
Helps the user add a shortcut to this assistant on their home screen. Shows a card in the conversation; when the user taps it, the launcher asks them to confirm adding the shortcut. Waits for the user. Use when the user asks to add this app or assistant to their home screen. The result's outcome is completed when the user finished it, declined when they turned it down or did not finish, failed when it could not be started, expired when they did not respond in time, not_shown when no conversation was on screen to show the card, already_done when nothing was needed, or unsupported when this device can't do it.
Helps the user make this app the device's default digital assistant. Shows a card in the conversation; when the user taps it, the system settings open where they choose the default assistant app. Waits for the user. Use when the user asks to make this app their default assistant or to open it with the assistant gesture or button. Call it even if the app may already be the default assistant; it then reports already_done without showing a card, so tell the user it is already set. The result's outcome is completed when the user finished it, declined when they turned it down or did not finish, failed when it could not be started, expired when they did not respond in time, not_shown when no conversation was on screen to show the card, already_done when nothing was needed, or unsupported when this device can't do it.
Helps the user update this app from Google Play. Shows a card in the conversation; when the user taps it, Google Play asks them to confirm, the update downloads in the background, and the app offers a restart when it is ready. Waits for the user. Use when the user asks to update the app. The result's outcome is completed when the user finished it, declined when they turned it down or did not finish, failed when it could not be started, expired when they did not respond in time, not_shown when no conversation was on screen to show the card, already_done when nothing was needed, or unsupported when this device can't do it. already_done here means the app is up to date. It can also be in_progress when an update is already downloading or downloaded and waiting for a restart, or use_play_store when the update can't run in the app (an earlier download failed or was cancelled, or Google Play doesn't allow it), in which case tell the user to update it from the Google Play Store. Call it even if the user turned an update down before; asking again shows the card again.

HorizontalTo(x=
Horizontally scrollable component was measured with an infinity maximum width constraints, which is disallowed. One of the common reasons is nesting layouts like LazyRow and Row(Modifier.horizontalScroll()). If you want to add a header before the list of items please add a header as a separate item() before the main items() inside the LazyRow scope. There could be other reasons for this to happen: your ComposeView was added into a LinearLayout with some weight, you applied Modifier.wrapContentSize(unbounded = true) or wrote a custom layout. Please try to remove the source of infinite constraints in the hierarchy above the scrolling container.

List the ALARMS set with alarm.set, from the app's own record of them. This is not the phone's full alarm list: Android doesn't let apps read the Clock app's alarms, so changes made directly in Clock are not reflected. An alarm the user created in Clock won't appear, and one they edited or deleted there may still be listed as it was. Use this before dismissing alarms by id, to confirm an alarm you set was saved correctly (including its trigger date/time), or when the user asks 'what alarms do I have?'. Returns { alarms: [...] } where each entry contains: id, label, hour, minute, trigger_time_ms (absolute epoch), trigger_time_iso (human-readable ISO-8601 in device local time), days, days_weekdays, vibrate, type ('ALARM'). For reminders use reminder.list.
List the reminders (alerts) currently set on one or more calendar events. Use this for 'What reminders are on my dentist appointment?' or before adding/removing an alert. Get the event_id from the `events` array of the `calendar` data source first. Always pass `targets_json`, a JSON array string of target objects, even for one event. Each object must include `event_id`. Returns each event's reminders with their `minutes_before`.

Photos
Photos on the user's device that matched. This is metadata only — no image content is included, so never describe what a photo depicts or claim to have looked at it. Report the time from `taken_at_local` (local wall-clock), the day from `taken_at_local_date`, and the weekday from `taken_at_weekday` verbatim. `has_capture_date` is false when the file carried no capture date — screenshots, downloads, and most PNGs — and the time shown is when the file was last written instead; in that case do not assert when the photo was taken. `access_scope` is 'selected' when the user granted access to only some photos, which means the library was NOT searched in full: say so rather than concluding none exist. `has_more` true means more photos matched than were returned: pass `next_offset` back as `offset` to reach older ones. When `labels` was used, `labels_available` false means the on-device model has not finished downloading, so content was NOT checked: say you could not look inside the photos yet rather than reporting none matched. `photos_scanned_for_labels` is how many were actually examined, `photos_unreadable` how many could not be opened at all and were therefore neither matched nor ruled out, and `label_scan_truncated` true means the scan stopped early, so absence is not proof. `location_available` false means photo location was not shared, so absent coordinates say nothing about where a photo was taken. `id` and `uri` are opaque handles for follow-up commands — never show either to the user. Only photos stored on this device were searched. Photos held solely in a cloud service such as Google Photos are not on the device and were not searched, so a photo the user expects may simply not be here: say that rather than saying it does not exist. If they want you to see such a photo, they can attach it directly in the composer.

Register a geofence so the device sends a proactive notification when the user arrives at or leaves a location. Use this when the user asks for location-based reminders (e.g. 'remind me when I get to the office', 'let me know when I leave home', 'notify me when I'm near the gym'). The geofence runs in the background with minimal battery impact and survives app backgrounding. IMPORTANT: Do NOT guess latitude/longitude coordinates for named places. Instead, provide the address and the device will geocode it to precise coordinates. You can provide either an address OR latitude/longitude. By default geofences are one-time (auto-removed after first trigger). IMPORTANT: Ask the user whether they want a one-time notification or ongoing monitoring before setting the geofence. Search or browse the device's calendars and return matching events. `start_date` is required. Pass `query` to find events by keyword — it does a typo-tolerant, accent-insensitive match across the event title, description, location, organizer, and attendees, and ranks the best matches first. Use it for requests like 'When is my dentist appointment?', 'Find my 1:1 with Sarah', 'Look for the budget review'. Omit `query` to simply list everything in a date range, for requests like 'What's on my calendar next week?' or 'Do I have anything Friday afternoon?'. `start_date` and `end_date` (ISO-8601) bound the window; when `end_date` is omitted, a keyword search spans two years from the start, and a plain browse defaults to one month from the start. Returns events with their id, title, start/end time, location, calendar, and recurrence info.
Search or browse the device's call log and return matching calls, most recent first. All parameters are optional. Pass `query` to filter by caller — it matches the cached contact name or the phone number. Use it for requests like 'When did I last call Sarah?' or 'Show my recent calls'. Omit `query` to list the most recent calls. `start_date` and `end_date` (ISO-8601) bound the window. Returns entries with number, name, direction, local date and time, and duration.
Search or browse the device's text messages (SMS / MMS / RCS) and return matching messages. All parameters are optional. Pass `query` to find messages by keyword — it does a typo-tolerant, accent-insensitive match against the message body (and sender/recipient address), ranking the best matches first. Use it for requests like 'What was that restaurant I mentioned to Alex?' or 'Find the text with the gate code'. Omit `query` to simply list the most recent messages, for requests like 'What did I text recently?'. Pass `contact` to restrict the search to the conversation with one person (a contact name or a phone number) — for 'what restaurant did I mention to Alex?' pass contact='Alex', query='restaurant'. `start_date` and `end_date` (ISO-8601) bound the window; when omitted, a keyword search covers roughly the last three months and a plain browse covers the last month. Returns messages with their address, body, timestamp, contact name, and attachment info. A `threadId` identifies a stored conversation on this device; it is not a phone number or contact ID and must not be passed as `recipients` or `contact_ids` when sending.
Search or browse the photos on the user's device and return what matches, most recent first. Returns metadata only — never image data — so it is cheap and safe to call before deciding which photos matter. All parameters are optional; omit them all to list the most recent photos. Use it for requests like 'my recent photos', 'photos from last Tuesday', 'shots from my Trips album', or 'my screenshots'.
Search results from the user's calendar. `start_date`/`end_date` are UTC and for internal use only — NEVER show them to the user and never use them to compute the day, date, or weekday. Display the date/time from the local fields instead: for a timed event (`is_all_day`=false) use `start_local`/`end_local` (the event's local wall-clock time); for an all-day event (`is_all_day`=true) use `start_local_date` (first day) through `end_local_date` (last day, INCLUSIVE) — note the UTC `end_date` is exclusive (midnight after the last day) and must not be shown. If `start_local_date` equals `end_local_date` it is a single all-day day. Always show the weekday using the provided `start_weekday`/`end_weekday` verbatim; never derive the weekday yourself.
Search results from the user's call log. Use `direction` — incoming, outgoing, missed, voicemail, rejected, blocked, or answered_externally — to say what kind of call it was; it is authoritative and must never be inferred from any other field. `outgoing` means the USER placed the call; only `missed` means they missed one. `type` and `date` are raw internal values — `type` is an Android enum integer and `date` is UTC epoch milliseconds. NEVER show either to the user, never fall back to `type` to determine direction, and never use `date` to compute the day, date, or weekday: it names the wrong day for calls made in the evening. Report the time from `date_local` (local wall-clock) and the day from `date_local_date`, and show the weekday using `date_weekday` verbatim. `duration` is in SECONDS. An entry records only that a call occurred — it says nothing about what was discussed, so never state or speculate about the topic, purpose, or outcome of a call.
Search results from the user's contacts, best match first. Ranking is fuzzy and matches organization, job title, email, note, address, and phone as well as the name, so the top result is a guess, not an answer — never treat it as the person the user meant just because it ranked first. `requiresUserChoice: true` means several saved people genuinely share the name that was searched for, and they are listed in `nameMatches`. When you see it, show the user those people by `displayName` and ask which one they mean. Where two of them share a `displayName` they are different people, so add something that tells them apart — the phone number, or the organization. Do NOT pick one yourself, and do not message or call anyone until they have answered. Once they choose, pass that person's `platformId` as `contact_ids` to `message.draft`, `message.send`, or the calling flow — never re-search by name. `nameMatchesTruncated: true` means `nameMatches` was capped and holds only some of the `nameMatchTotal` people who share that name — say so when you present the list, and ask the user for a fuller name to search instead of implying these are all of them.
Search results from the user's text messages. `direction` is authoritative for who sent a message — `inbound` means the other party sent it to the user, `outbound` means the user sent it. `address` and `contactName` identify the other party: the sender for inbound messages and the recipient for outbound messages. Do not infer the author from `contactName` alone. `timestampMs` is UTC epoch milliseconds and for internal use only — NEVER show it to the user and never use it to compute the day, date, or weekday: it names the wrong day for messages sent in the evening. Report the time from `timestamp_local` (local wall-clock) and the day from `timestamp_local_date`, and show the weekday using `timestamp_weekday` verbatim. A message with an MMS/RCS attachment carries an `attachments` array; each entry has an `attachmentId`, `type`, `mimeType`, and `filename`. An entry that already has an `uploadedPath` can be retrieved at that path. An entry without one is still on the phone and has NOT been read — do not tell the user you cannot access it. Call `message.attachment.get` with its `attachmentId` to fetch it, then read the `uploadedPath` that command returns. `resultOrder` tells you how `messages` is sorted: `newest_first` when you omit `query` (a plain browse), `relevance` when you pass one. `truncated: true` means `returnedCount` was capped and you have NOT seen the whole window — never conclude a message does not exist from a truncated result. When `resultOrder` is `newest_first`, everything older than `oldestReturned` was cut off, so re-query with `end_date` set to `oldestReturned` to page backwards. When it is `relevance` there is no time cut-off — the messages you did not see are the lower-scoring ones, anywhere in the window — so narrow with `contact` or a shorter date range instead, never with `oldestReturned`. `attachmentCandidates` lists recent messages in the same window that carry a photo, voice note, or file but did NOT match your keywords — because an attachment's contents cannot be searched until they are read. A caption-less photo of a receipt or invoice appears ONLY here, never in `messages`. When the user is asking about something that would live inside an image or document, fetch these with `message.attachment.get` and read them before answering or saying you found nothing.
Search the device's contacts by keyword and return matching people. `query` is required — it does a typo-tolerant, accent-insensitive match across the contact's name, organization, job title, email, note, postal address, and phone number, and ranks the best matches first. Use it for requests like 'What's Sarah's number?', 'Find my dentist's contact', 'Who do I know at Acme?'. Prefer this over reading the full contacts data source when looking for specific people — it returns a small ranked result instead of the entire address book.

Set a new alarm on the user's device. The alarm appears in the device clock app and rings there; on a device with no clock app it falls back to an in-app alarm that rings with the device alarm tone. Use this for anything the user calls an alarm or a wake-up, including relative ones: 'Set an alarm for 7am', 'Wake me up at 6:30', 'Set an alarm for 10 minutes from now', 'Wake me in 20 minutes', or 'Set a recurring alarm for weekdays at 8am'. Prefer this over reminder.set whenever the user says 'alarm' or 'wake me', even when the time is only minutes away. An alarm has no relative-offset field: for 'in N minutes/hours', add N to the current device time and pass the resulting absolute `hour` and `minutes`. For repeats beyond a weekday mask, pass `frequency` ('DAILY', 'WEEKLY', 'MONTHLY', 'YEARLY') with an optional `interval`, and bound it with `count` or `until`; such alarms are driven in-app since the system clock app only supports a weekday mask. Always pass `alarms_json`, a JSON array string of alarm objects, even for one alarm. Each object must include `hour` and `minutes`; optional per-alarm fields are `message`, `days`, `vibrate`, `frequency`, `interval`, `count`, `until`, and `timezone` (an IANA id; defaults to the device time zone).
Set a new reminder on the user's device. The reminder is saved as an event in the user's calendar, whose alert notifies at the chosen time. When the phone can't do that (no calendar app, calendar access off, or no calendar account), it sets nothing and returns an error; then offer to set the reminder yourself as a chat reminder. Reminders are distinct from alarms, which ring through the system clock app. If the user says 'alarm' or 'wake me', use alarm.set instead, even when the time is relative like 'in 10 minutes'. Use this for requests like 'Remind me to stretch in 2 hours', 'Remind me to take my medicine at 3pm', 'Remind me every weekday at 9am to stand up', or 'Remind me to call mom on May 15 at 9am' (supply date='2026-05-15' for future-dated reminders more than 24 hours away). For richer repeats, pass `frequency` ('DAILY', 'WEEKLY', 'MONTHLY', 'YEARLY') with an optional `interval` (e.g. frequency='DAILY', interval=3 for every 3 days). Bound a repeating reminder with `count` (total number of times) or `until` (ISO-8601 end date); for MONTHLY/YEARLY pass `date` as the start so the day-of-month is anchored. Always pass `reminders_json`, a JSON array string of reminder objects, even for one reminder. Each object must include `hour` and `minutes`; optional per-reminder fields are `message`, `days`, `date`, `frequency`, `interval`, `count`, `until`, and `timezone` (an IANA id like 'America/Los_Angeles'; defaults to the device time zone).

Suggest that the user let the app keep running in the background so it can continue a long-running task even after they leave the app. Use this when a task requires waiting for and reacting to incoming events over time — e.g. texting back and forth with a customer-service agent over SMS where replies take minutes, watching for a message or status change, or any multi-step task you cannot finish in a single turn. This requires the user's "Run in background" permission. If it is not yet enabled, calling this returns a message with a card link you must relay to the user verbatim — it shows an Enable button that turns it on; the task is not protected until they enable it. You do NOT start, extend, or end background running — once the user enables it the app keeps running in the background until the user turns it off. Turn on torch
Turn the Live avatar off. Shorthand for ui.set.voice.set_live_avatar with live_avatar_status="off"; prefer that command, which can also turn the Live avatar back on. Writes the same saved Voice Controls "Live avatar" setting, so it stays off for later calls until it is turned back on. The call keeps running, the microphone and audio are untouched, and the agent's still avatar image stays on screen; only the live animated avatar stops.
Turn the Live avatar on or off during an active voice call. Writes the saved Voice Controls "Live avatar" setting, so the choice also applies to later calls until it is changed again. The call keeps running, the microphone and audio are untouched, and the agent's still avatar image stays on screen either way. Turning it off stops the live animated avatar immediately; turning it on shows it again only if this call started with the Live avatar on, otherwise it starts with the next call. Use for "turn the live avatar off/on", "stop/start animating", or "disable/enable personification".

Update Preview stream state to 
Update an existing calendar event. Only the fields you provide will be changed; omitted fields stay the same. Use this for requests like 'Move my 3pm meeting to 4pm', 'Change the location of my lunch meeting', 'Rename my afternoon event', 'Make my standup repeat every weekday', 'Remind me 15 minutes before'. Get the event_id from the `events` array of the `calendar` data source first. Pass `rrule` (with optional `duration`, ISO-8601, default 'PT1H') to make an event repeat — do not also pass `end_time` in that case. Pass `reminder_minutes` to set the alert lead time (replaces existing reminders), `timezone` to change the event time zone, or `calendar_id` to move the event to another calendar. For a recurring event, passing an occurrence's composite id ('<id>#<occurrence ISO date>') edits just that occurrence (only `title`, `start_time`, `end_time`, `description`, `location`, `all_day` apply); pass the bare numeric id or `scope`='all_events' to change the whole series. Always pass `updates_json`, a JSON array string of update objects, even for one event. Each object must include `event_id` and may include `scope` ('this_event' or 'all_events'); optional per-event fields are `title`, `start_time`, `end_time`, `description`, `location`, `all_day`, `rrule`, `duration`, `reminder_minutes`, `timezone`, and `calendar_id`.

When true, non-phone/non-email values in `recipients` are looked up as contact names. A name is never messaged directly: every match is returned for the user to pick from, or — when only one contact matched — to confirm, after which you call again with that `contact_id` in `contact_ids`. Name matching is fuzzy, so a single match is not proof it is the right person.
When true, return only photos the user marked as favorites. Not available on Android 10; the call fails with `unsupported_filter` there rather than ignoring it. Optional.
Where the file came from. Exactly one of: 'camera' (taken with this device's camera), 'screenshot', 'download' (saved from the web or another app), 'received' (arrived through a messaging app such as WhatsApp, Messenger or Telegram). Any other value is rejected. This describes the file's origin, not its subject. Omit it unless the user named an origin: most libraries hold far more received photos than camera ones, so filtering to 'camera' can hide the majority of the device. Optional.

Who to send to. Two accepted shapes: a comma-separated list of raw phone numbers (e.g. "+15551234567") / email addresses, or a JSON array of objects that may also carry a name, e.g. '[{"address":"+15551234567","name":"Natasha"}]'. `name` is only a display label for the card and never changes who is messaged — the message is always addressed by `address` — and whether to set it depends on this device's Contacts permission, covered next. Values that are neither a phone number nor an email are treated as contact names only when `resolve_name` is true; otherwise the entire request is rejected. Every recipient must resolve before anything is sent. For a known contact prefer `contact_ids`. Pass this parameter as a string, not a JSON array. Never use a message ID or thread ID as an address.

Words
Words to match against on-device image labels. The classifier can only emit labels from the fixed list below, so choose from it rather than guessing: a word that is not in the list can never match. Pick the closest available labels for what the user asked - a wristwatch is Clock or Bracelet, a beach scene may be Beach, Sand, Shore or Surfboard. Matching is substring and case-insensitive and a photo matches if any word matches, so pass several related labels. uniform 
uniform float2 bkResolution;

uniform float4 bkRenderMargin;

uniform int passIndex;

uniform mat4 uTexMatrix;
uniform mat4 uTransMatrix;
attribute vec4 aPosition;
attribute vec4 aTextureCoord;
varying vec2 %s;
void main() {
    gl_Position = uTransMatrix * aPosition;
    %s = (uTexMatrix * aTextureCoord).xy;
}

uniform mat4 uTransMatrix;
attribute vec4 aPosition;
void main() {
    gl_Position = uTransMatrix * aPosition;
}

uniform sampler2D y_tex;
uniform sampler2D u_tex;
uniform sampler2D v_tex;
vec4 sample(vec2 p) {
  float y = texture2D(y_tex, p).r * 1.16438;
  float u = texture2D(u_tex, p).r;
  float v = texture2D(v_tex, p).r;
  return vec4(y + 1.59603 * v - 0.874202,
    y - 0.391762 * u - 0.812968 * v + 0.531668,
    y + 2.01723 * u - 1.08563, 1);
}

uniform shader inputImage;

uniform shader inputImage;
uniform float2 bkClampMin;
uniform float2 bkClampMax;
half4 main(float2 coord) {
  return inputImage.eval(clamp(coord, bkClampMin, bkClampMax));
}

uniform vec2 xUnit;
uniform vec4 coeffs;

void main() {
  gl_FragColor.r = coeffs.a + dot(coeffs.rgb,
      sample(tc - 1.5 * xUnit).rgb);
  gl_FragColor.g = coeffs.a + dot(coeffs.rgb,
      sample(tc - 0.5 * xUnit).rgb);
  gl_FragColor.b = coeffs.a + dot(coeffs.rgb,
      sample(tc + 0.5 * xUnit).rgb);
  gl_FragColor.a = coeffs.a + dot(coeffs.rgb,
      sample(tc + 1.5 * xUnit).rgb);
}
